//: The WEB half of the platform-split typecheck (`npm run typecheck`);
tsconfig.native.json is the other half. The pattern's whole point is that
each per-component index re-exports the extensionless './<name>' and the
consumer's bundler picks the leaf — so tsc must be taught the same trick:
button.web.tsx here, exactly as Vite does. The native config flips it
to ['.native', ''] for Metro's view of the same imports.
- `moduleResolution: Bundler` overrides the base's NodeNext, which
rejects extensionless relative imports outright and would never reach
the suffix list. Bundler is the truthful mode: this package has no
build step and is only ever consumed by bundlers (Vite, Metro).
The .native.tsx leaves are excluded — they are the other program. Both
configs extend the strict base; nothing there is loosened.
